messages:
infra-alert-bot: Paging oncall for PROD streaming tail-latency spike. Severity: P2. Affected service: hosted-api-prod /stream SSE endpoints. Alert: p99 > 2s for last 5m, streaming stalls rising. Incident created: auto-INC-2026-3248 :rotating_light:

oncall_anna: I'm on it. forwarding to SRE.
sre_jon: seeing the same in grafana - spike started ~1809990900 (~5m ago). p95 jumped to ~430ms (baseline ~120ms), p99 ~2.4s (baseline ~350ms). Streaming stall rate (chunk gap > 1s) ~12%.
runtime_lee: quick question — is this only SSE or websocket too?
sre_jon: both appear elevated but SSE endpoints show more chunking. headers show repeated "502 from streaming-proxy" in traces.
support_maya: we already had a customer message: @customer_jim reported partial responses and reconnects for a small subset of sessions. He pasted session id: sess-9f3a.
customer_jim: confirmed. session sess-9f3a stalled, client retried and got duplicate chunks on reconnect. Impact: a few enterprise customers reported degraded UX.
oncall_anna: can someone grab proxy logs and tail the streaming-proxy pods?
sre_jon: doing: ```kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=streaming-proxy -o wide``` then ```kubectl -n prod logs -f deploy/streaming-proxy --since=10m | grep -E "chunk|timeout|reset|backpressure"```
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline note: no recent streaming-proxy deploys in last 24h.
runtime_lee: grabbing metrics from edge-proxy as well: saw increased buffer occupancy on the SSE worker queues. KV cache hit rates are normal. There are bursts of slow consumer backpressure from downstream clients.
sre_jon: paste from logs: ```[1809991202] WARN stream: slow consumer detected, write timeout 1.2s, client=10.3.12.45, session=sess-9f3a
[1809991210] ERROR proxy: upstream reset, code=ECONNRESET, model=redwood-v1-large
[1809991219] WARN chunker: chunk delay 1500ms, session=sess-7b2c
[1809991230] INFO stream: reconnect attempt by client sess-9f3a```
support_maya: customers affected: 3 enterprise accounts reported via CS in last 10m. impact: intermittent truncated streams and delayed finalizing tokens.
runtime_lee: hypothesis: client-level backpressure + proxy write timeout default 1s. If many clients are slow, proxy worker threads clog and increase tail latency. Also noticed number of open connections rising 30% above baseline.
oncall_anna: mitigation plan: 1) increase streaming-proxy write timeout to 3s temporarily, 2) scale streaming-proxy replicas + ephemeral burst workers, 3) enable aggressive keepalive/queue drop for very slow clients, 4) fallback model routing for heavy sessions. I'll coordinate.
sre_jon: I'll spin up an extra 3 replicas: ```kubectl -n prod scale deploy/streaming-proxy --replicas=8``` doing now.
sre_jon: scaling... replicas increased to 8.
deploy-bot: HorizontalPodAutoscaler: target CPU 60%, current 82% -> scaling recommended.
time 1809991305 runtime_lee: changing write timeout in configmap and rolling restart: ```kubectl -n prod set env deploy/streaming-proxy PROXY_WRITE_TIMEOUT=3000 && kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/streaming-proxy``` proceeding.
sre_jon: restart in progress. watching logs.
(some minutes pass)
sre_jon: after scale + timeout bump: p95 down to ~160ms, p99 down to ~520ms, streaming stall rate dropped from 12% to ~2.5% in 2m window.
oncall_anna: good sign. are we seeing any errors from model servers?
runtime_lee: model servers show some transient 503s earlier correlated with proxy resets but nothing ongoing. KV cache sizes stable.
support_maya: CS updated affected customers with a short note and workaround (retry on reconnect). No escalations yet.
customer_jim: got the follow-up — latency improved on our end. Thanks for the quick fix.
sre_jon: will keep monitoring for 30 more minutes, then demote to P3 and start postmortem.
oncall_anna: logging incident details and tagging for postmortem: root-cause candidate = client slow-consumer amplification + conservative proxy timeout causing worker stall under burst. Actions: scale, timeout bump, investigate long tail sessions, add queue-drop policy, perf test with synthetic slow clients.
infra-alert-bot: Incident auto-update: INC-2026-3248 status=mitigated assignee=@oncall_anna severity=P2 created=1809991234 mitigated=1809991398
sre_jon: creating CR to increase default PROXY_WRITE_TIMEOUT to 2.5s for next rollout and add metrics for slow-consumer queue depth.
oncall_anna: assigning postmortem to runtime team + SRE. I'll own the remediation EPIC.
deploy-bot: Note: rolling restart finished at 1809991328, no failed pods.
runtime_lee: quick note — I'll also add a streaming smoke test that simulates a 100ms token delay followed by a 2s pause to ensure backpressure behavior is safe.
sre_jon: closing loop: p99 now ~480ms, stall rate steady ~2%. I'll keep an eye for the next 20m.
oncall_anna: thanks all. tagging docs: #inc-2026-3248, will write a short blameless postmortem template. :white_check_mark:
